title: Prefill Coordinator scrumlet notes - staged lanes and hit-ratio v2
body:
Scrumlet: Prefill Coordinator sync — 2028-03-12
Attendees: Priya (chair), Ethan, Marta, Kunal, Sam, Aisha (joined late)
Channel refs: #serving-runtime, #infra-prefetch, slack thread: /thread/C12F9K
Agenda:
- Quick status on prefill rollout canary
- New idea: staged prefill lanes (hot/warm/cold) and admission policy
- Hit-ratio v2 metric definition + telemetry gaps
- Kernel backpressure observed on long-seq tails
- Action items & owners

Notes / Observations:
1) Canary update:
   - Canary running on 12 nodes (g5x2) for the past 36h, traffic mirrored at 5% from prod routes INF-hosted-A.
   - Prefill hit ratio (old definition) improved from 18% -> 29% in steady windows, cost estimate down ~7% for mirrored traffic.
   - However, observed 95th tail latency bump on kernels serving long prefix (seq_len > 1024) during a burst at 03:20 UTC. Trace shows kernel handshake stalls when coalescer tries to prefetch overlapping KV windows.
   - Sam traced to scheduling starvation for microkernel with async prefill; PR4021 mitigates one race but not scheduling contention.

2) Staged prefill lanes proposal (brain-dump):
   - Split prefill traffic into lanes: hot (recently-accessed prefixes, aggressive prefill), warm (heuristic score 0.5-0.8, limited prefill window), cold (low prob, no prefill, only opportunistic caching).
   - Admission policy: lane decision made at router layer using per-key recent-access TTL + model sequence-length heuristic. This reduces wasted KV fill for seldom-used prefixes.
   - Expected benefits: fewer kernel handoffs for cold keys, reduced memory churn on KV store, better batching cohesion in hot lane.
   - Risks: incorrect lane assignment may increase latency for some long-running chats; needs rollback-able rollout.

3) Hit-ratio v2 (metrics refinement):
   - Problem with current "prefill_hit_ratio": it conflates short-term warmups and long_prefix reuses. Need two signals: 
     * prefill_hit_ratio_recent: fraction of requests where prefilled KV was used within 60s window
     * prefill_hit_ratio_sequence_reuse: fraction where identical prefix sequence reused within model call (helps measure exact reuse)
   - Additional metric: prefill_waste_bytes: bytes pushed into KV but evicted without any hits within TTL. This informs wasted memory and network egress.
   - Telemetry gaps: agent rollout doesn't emit sequence-level hashes for privacy reasons; propose a rolling-hash fingerprint (non-reversible) to attach to metrics (see INF-5019).

4) Kernel/backpressure notes:
   - Kunal ran microbench for async prefill and saw kernel queue depth spike when too many overlapping prefill tasks were scheduled.
   - We should cap concurrent async-prefill tasks per-core and prefer batching on the coalescer to create larger, fewer kernel calls.
   - Short-term: add soft quota in scheduler for async prefill tasks and fallback to on-demand KV fill when quota exceeded.

5) Experiment ideas & quick wins:
   - A: Implement staged lanes in router as a feature-flagged path; mirror but do not serve traffic until canary passes 48h without >10% tail-latency regression.
   - B: Emit prefill_waste_bytes in canary, run nightly job to compute cost delta across mirrored traffic.
   - C: Kernel scheduler change: PR4021 + soft quota, measure kernel-sched-wait histogram.
   - D: Heuristic tweak: for seq_len > 2048 treat as "long-seq" and limit prefill window to 128 tokens to reduce KV size.

Decisions made:
- Greenlight staged-lanes prototype behind flag (pri: Priya + Kunal). Start with hot/warm/cold simple scoring; no ML model initially.
- Add prefill_waste_bytes and the two hit-ratio signals to our canary telemetry (owner: Marta).
- Immediate kernel protection: soft quota on async-prefill tasks (owner: Sam).

Action items (owner - due):
- Priya: land router flag scaffolding for lanes, include toggle for mirror/active switch. (due 2028-03-19)
- Kunal: implement lane scoring function (TTL + access_count heuristic) + unit tests. (due 2028-03-18)
- Marta: add metrics (prefill_waste_bytes, hit-ratio-recent, hit-ratio-seq) to canary pipeline; update Grafana dashboards. (due 2028-03-16)
- Sam: add soft quota + kernel-sched-wait histogram instrumentation in PR4021 followup. (due 2028-03-15)
- Ethan: run cost-simulation on mirrored dataset to estimate savings for staged lanes, produce short spreadsheet. (due 2028-03-20)
- Aisha: audit privacy for rolling-hash fingerprint approach (INF-5019) and confirm compliance with KMS policy. (due 2028-03-17)

Open questions / risks:
- How to choose TTL thresholds for lane scoring without causing oscillation? Need a small A/B matrix in canary.
- Prefill fingerprint design: must be non-reversible, low-entropy collision risk acceptable? Legal needs sign-off.
- Impact on Dedicated customers with pinned model versions — we need to ensure lane logic respects model pinned variants and quantized kernels.

Notes to self / TODOs in doc:
- Add link to nightly cost job once Ethan shares spreadsheet.
- Sketch a migration plan if staged lanes cause a regression: immediate disable -> degrade to on-demand prefill -> rollback kernel changes.

Next sync: quick check-in Mon 2028-03-14 11:00 PT if metrics start coming in, otherwise standard scrumlet next Friday 2028-03-19.

References / quick links:
- PR4021 (partial fix for race): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4021
- Lane prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/compare/prefill-lanes
- JIRA tickets: INF-4872 (canary rollout), INF-5019 (telemetry privacy)

Minutes saved as draft — please add notes inline if you were on the call or saw mirrored logs.

-- Priya
